jess-customer: Hey team — starting ~09:47 UTC our clients started getting 429s after we rotated our billing card. Same traffic, same users. Error body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded"}. We're behind a cloud NAT (single egress IP). Any idea why this would coincide with billing rotation? cc @sara-support

sara-support: Sorry about that. Can you paste the raw response headers (not the full key) and one example request log line? Also whether you include X-Forwarded-For or any client-identifying header.

jess-customer: Sample response headers below (redacted):
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Thu, 28 Dec 2023 09:48:40 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 3000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1709123600
X-Request-ID: req_abc123
X-Auth-Scheme: api_key

And our gateway log snippet (redacted):
2023-12-28T09:47:55Z svc-web-01 POST /v1/complete 429 auth="missing" remote_addr=34.12.56.78 xfwd_for="10.0.2.15" key_id=old-key-id

We rotated the key at 09:40 via dashboard; clients got new key seconds later, but some workers still had the old key for ~10m.

mike-sre: Quick taxonomy: quota attribution order is typically api_key -> project -> org -> ip (NAT bucket) depending on auth header parsing and trust chain. If a request arrives unauthenticated (or header dropped by a proxy), it falls back to the egress-IP bucket. NATed fleets can blow that bucket fast.

sara-support: @jess-customer can you confirm the Authorization header format you sent (Authorization: Bearer <token> vs Authorization: Api-Key <key>) and whether any edge proxy might rewrite headers?

jess-customer: We use Authorization: Api-Key <key>. Our env var update swapped the key but one kube pod was still running the old image and hit 429s. I also noticed some logs that show auth parsing failed: "auth="missing""

leo-eng: looking at proxy traces now — I can repro a header-strip: our legacy gateway (edge-proxy v1.9) has a bug where Authorization values containing a colon (:) get truncated/dropped after a parsing refactor. That will make the request look unauthenticated and cause IP-level rate attribution. Repro steps I used: 

1) curl without Authorization -> 429 with header X-RateLimit-Scope: ip
2) curl with Authorization: Api-Key ab:cd:ef -> gateway logs show header dropped -> 429 w/ ip scope

Example repro: 

```
curl -v -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -H "Authorization: Api-Key ab:cd:ef" \
     https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```
Gateway log: ``auth=\"missing\" remote_addr=34.12.56.78``

rl-ratebot: automated: Detected spike: 4,120 429s attributed to 34.12.56.78 between 09:46 and 09:56 UTC (limit window 60s, per-ip limit 3k/min).

mike-sre: That lines up — while the key rotation happened, a subset of pods sent requests that the proxy treated as unauthenticated. Because you sit behind one NAT IP, the burst bumped the IP bucket and clients saw 429s. Not related to billing rotation directly.

sara-support: Action items: 
- leo-eng to patch proxy to stop dropping Authorization with colons (PR #4321). ETA ~2h.
- temporary mitigation: we increased the per-IP bucket for 34.12.56.78 by +50% for the next 1 hour to avoid more consumer-facing 429s.
- customer to restart the stale pods / rotate key again to ensure all instances use the new key.
- support to offer a one-time quota bump if needed and advise dedicated capacity if predictable spikes continue.

leo-eng: submitted fix PR, rolling restart scheduled for edge-proxy group in region-us-east-1 in 15m. Also added a guard to log Authorization parsing failures as metric.

jess-customer: restarting pods now. Also re-rotated API key (created new key and updated env). I can share a curl after restart.

(10 minutes later)
jess-customer: Confirmed 429s stopped after restart and new key. Traffic looks normal. Thanks everyone! :tada:

sara-support: Great — closing the incident unless anything else pops up. If you want, we can open a follow-up to look at moving you onto dedicated capacity or a per-key guarantee to avoid IP-bucket fallbacks in future.
